title: Event listeners at the class level don't organize well for subclasses

labels.name: events
labels.description: SQLAlchemy event hooks, the event system

body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/8466

symptom: "SessionEvent listener not called if registered before `sessionmaker`"

the patch below shows where it goes wrong for this particular case:

```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/event/attr.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/event/attr.py
index f8d70a06a6..cf4c38cb52 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/event/attr.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/event/attr.py
@@ -210,11 +210,16 @@ class _ClsLevelDispatch(RefCollection[_ET]):
                 self.update_subclass(cls)
             else:
                 if cls not in self._clslevel:
-                    self._assign_cls_collection(cls)
+                    self._assign_cls_collection(cls, warn=True)
                 self._clslevel[cls].append(event_key._listen_fn)
         registry._stored_in_collection(event_key, self)
 
-    def _assign_cls_collection(self, target: Type[_ET]) -> None:
+    def _assign_cls_collection(self, target: Type[_ET], warn: bool=False) -> None:
+        if warn:
+            for sup in target.__mro__[1:]:
+                if sup in self._clslevel:
+                    util.warn(f"about to lose events from superclass {sup}")
+
         if getattr(target, "_sa_propagate_class_events", True):
             self._clslevel[target] = collections.deque()
```

test case below illustrates two combinations.  Note that sessionmaker() makes a subclass of Session, so this test simulates that.

```py
from sqlalchemy import event
from unittest import mock

class SomeBaseClass(event.EventTarget):
    pass


class SomeEvents(event.Events):
    _dispatch_target = SomeBaseClass

    def some_event(self):
        pass


def test_case_one():
    clslevel = mock.Mock()
    subclslevel = mock.Mock()

    event.listen(SomeBaseClass, "some_event", clslevel)

    class SomeSubClass(SomeBaseClass):
        pass

    event.listen(SomeSubClass, "some_event", subclslevel)


    ssc = SomeSubClass()
    ssc.dispatch.some_event('x')

    assert clslevel.mock_calls == [mock.call('x')]
    assert subclslevel.mock_calls == [mock.call('x')]

def test_case_two():

    clslevel = mock.Mock()
    subclslevel = mock.Mock()

    class SomeSubClass(SomeBaseClass):
        pass

    event.listen(SomeBaseClass, "some_event", clslevel)
    event.listen(SomeSubClass, "some_event", subclslevel)

    ssc = SomeSubClass()
    ssc.dispatch.some_event('x')

    assert clslevel.mock_calls == [mock.call('x')]
    assert subclslevel.mock_calls == [mock.call('x')]
```
